scvw.passage: The SCV Water Board of Directors consists of nine directly elected directors, from three electoral divisions equally representing all corners of the Santa Clarita Valley. Elections are held each even-numbered year and the term of office for all elected Directors is four years. Kathye Armitage - Director; Ken Cooper - Director; William Cooper - Vice President; Maria Gutzeit - President; Dirk S. Marks - Director; Gary R. Martin - Vice President; Dan Masnada - Director; Piotr Orzechowski - Director; Kenneth J. Petersen, P.E. - Director.

khts.passage: Posted by: Jade Aubuchon in Santa Clarita Elections, Santa Clarita Latest News August 4, 2026 - 12:39 pm. Bill Cooper has announced his campaign for re-election to the Santa Clarita Valley Water Agency Board of Directors, representing Division 1. The election will be held Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. [...] Cooper is a career water professional, not a career politician. He worked for the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California for about 40 years and served in several leadership positions, including Water Treatment Section Manager. In that role, Cooper helped oversee the operation and maintenance of Metropolitan’s five major water treatment plants, which serve millions of Southern California residents. Cooper also taught water treatment courses at College of the Canyons, helping prepare students for careers in the water industry. His service on local water boards began in 1993 with the former Castaic Lake Water Agency. He served as president of that board for five years and later helped bring Santa Clarita’s three former water organizations together to form the SCV Water Agency. Cooper became the new agency’s first board president and helped guide the organization through its early years. Today, Cooper serves as a vice president of the SCV Water Board and chairs its Engineering and Operations Committee. He also serves on the Water Resources and Watershed Committee. [...] Cooper is also a United States Navy veteran who completed three tours during the Vietnam War. He and his family moved to Santa Clarita in 1972. [Family sentence omitted.] [...] Ed. Note: The above information was provided to KHTS Radio by Bill Cooper.

campaign.passage: Bill Cooper is a long time water professional and has worked for the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California for almost 40 years. During that time he has held various posts including the Water Treatment Section Manager overseeing the operations and maintenance of all five Metropolitan Water Treatment Plants that supply about one-half of all the water to the 19 million people in Southern California. Bill has managed some of the largest water treatment plants in the United States. He was an adjunct Professor at College of the Canyons teaching their Environmental Technologies Water Treatment Program. Bill has served on the CLWA Board since 1993 and was President of the Board for five year from 1996 to 2001. Since then, he has served on various committees and was the chair of the Planning and Engineering Committee which provided oversight of the Agency’s $55 million Capital Improvement Program. He is currently serving as CWLA Board Vice President. An active participant in the Santa Clarita Valley community, Bill is a member of the Child and Family Center Governing Board and currently serves as the Board Chairman. Bill is also a member of the Child and Family Centers Foundation Board and was the board chair from 2005 to 2006. Additionally, he was appointed by Santa Clarita Mayor Frank Ferry to the City’s Elected Officials Committee on teenage alcohol and drug abuse and was a member of the Sulphur Springs District Schools Site Council.
